title: Seller Performance Standing and the Northloop Payments Scheduled Payout Limit
content:
The payout limit of a Northloop Payments scheduled payout is scaled by the standing payout-limit multiplier, which turns on the seller's current level in Seller Performance Standing and, at the two highest levels, on the sale credits booked on the payments account in the last twelve months.

**Rule.** The standing payout-limit multiplier is 1.5 when the seller's current performance standing level is Top Rated Level or Preferred Partner Level and the sale credits booked on the account in the last twelve months total at least 250000 USD (250,000 USD); it is 0.8 when the level is Standard Level or Above Standard Level; it is 0.5 when the level is Below Standard Level or Developing Seller Level; otherwise it is 1.

A window of the last twelve months takes in the ledger entries dated after the same calendar day twelve months before the payout date, up to and including the payout date.

## Ladder

| Current Seller Performance Standing level | Sale credits of the last twelve months | Standing payout-limit multiplier |
|---|---|---|
| Top Rated Level or Preferred Partner Level | at least 250000 USD | 1.5 |
| Top Rated Level or Preferred Partner Level | below 250000 USD | 1 |
| Standard Level or Above Standard Level | any amount | 0.8 |
| Below Standard Level or Developing Seller Level | any amount | 0.5 |

The level is the seller's current level on the Seller Performance Standing record; the sale credits are the sale credit entries on the Northloop Payments ledger in the twelve-month window.

## Hypothetical boundary cases

- Top Rated Level with sale credits of exactly 250000.00 USD in the window: at least 250000 USD, so the multiplier is 1.5.
- Preferred Partner Level with 249999.99 USD: below the threshold, so the multiplier is 1.
- Above Standard Level with 900000.00 USD: the sale credits do not enter this tier, and the multiplier is 0.8.
